title: Undo the accidental edit
hook: Undo and redo walk the local edit history in opposite directions.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Restore a prior local edit and then reapply it.

objective: Restore a prior local edit and then reapply it.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Undo and redo walk the local edit history in opposite directions. Which command returns to the prior edit state? Correct option: Undo. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Undo returns to the previous stored state and redo reapplies that state transition. Apps differ in which operations and histories support these commands.
claims.source: Derivation from the explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and transformations in src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts; app documentation below provides command/filter context, not evidence of productivity gains or of every fixture-specific choice. Microsoft Learn, Keyboard accelerators, Common Keyboard Accelerators and scope caveats; retrieved 2026-10-13: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/input/keyboard-accelerators . Shortcuts depend on app, platform and locale; this exercise models the command, not a global keyboard binding. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: edit. Local command model; app and locale can differ. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, undo-then-redo fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. recall.question: A word reads 'cat'. In one edit you change it to 'dog', then press Undo, then Redo. What does it read?
recall.why: Undo steps back to 'cat'; Redo reapplies the change to 'dog'.
